question: Do you think children should have their own smartphones?
question_zh: 你认为孩子应该有自己的智能手机吗？
original_answer: yeah, I think it depends depends how the children self-disciplining ability developed. you know, I think maybe in general, there's a age range. for example, if you are under like 16 or 18, then you should have a limited on using smartphones. but actually, I think age doesn't stand for everything, because different children have different parents, and the parents' education method is different. So, if a parents are good at educating, and maybe their children will be, you know, more self-discipline, then they could have their own smartphone quickly. Because we all know that smartphone is a double-edged sword. So, if you think your children is able to control this sword, and use it to benefit your life, then I think you could have your own own smartphone. but I think both of the children's don't have ability. So, II if I recommend children's at least in primary school should not have their own smartphones. actually, I have my own smartphone in 2016 when I'm in, when I'm about to graduate from primary school and going to the junior school.

fixes.wrong: it depends how the children self-disciplining ability developed
fixes.right: It really depends on how well a kid can discipline themselves.
fixes.rule: depend on 加 how well 加完整从句；别把名词短语硬塞进动词后面。
stand for 是代表缩写的意思；年龄说明不了一切，直接说 age isn't everything。

fixes.wrong: I have my own smartphone in 2016
fixes.right: I got my first smartphone in 2016.
fixes.rule: 过去的时间点配过去式；第一台手机，用 got my first smartphone。

model_answer: It really depends on how well a kid can discipline themselves—that would be my honest first answer. My default position is no: kids in primary school shouldn't own a smartphone, and parents should set clear limits on screen time instead. But age isn't everything, because different children have different parents, and the parenting style makes a huge difference. We all know a smartphone is a double-edged sword: if a kid is mature enough to control it, it becomes a useful tool; if not, they'll just end up glued to the screen. For what it's worth, I got my first smartphone in 2016, right before junior high, and that timing worked pretty well for me.

titles: 孩子几岁该有手机？8.5 分的雅思答案，第一句就赢了一半
雅思 Part 3 杀手题：该给孩子买手机吗？别说 yes 或 no
考官问 Should kids have smartphones？一个句式直接把答案拉到 7 分以上
script_en: [curious] Should children have their own smartphones? Yes or no?
Most people pick a side. Band 8 answers refuse to—and here's the exact sentence they open with.
It really depends on how well a kid can discipline themselves.
Wait—so the answer is... no answer?

No, the answer is a condition. Primary schoolers? No—parents should set clear limits on screen time instead. But age isn't everything: good parenting changes everything, because a smartphone is a double-edged sword.
So don't defend a position—define the condition.
Exactly. It really depends on how well a kid can discipline themselves. Either way—set clear limits.
What would YOUR answer be? Comment below.
script_zh_variant: 考官问：孩子该有自己的手机吗？中国考生的第一反应是 yes 或 no——从这句话开始就已经输了。
It really depends on how well a kid can discipline themselves.
听到没有，第一句不给立场，给条件。这就是七分和六点五的分水岭。后面再加一句：
Parents should set clear limits on screen time.
家长该对屏幕时间设明确限制。一个条件，一个方案，三十秒，答案立住了。完整版在音频里。你的答案是什么？评论区交作业。
